externalProductDependencies.reason: beads is the issue tracker that ships underneath: it holds the work items, cooks and pours formulas, and owns every command dotdiw forwards. dotdiw adds discovery and hides the second name. It is reached only through the beads adapter, behind the tracker door; the interface is what dotdiw's bodies see.
externalProductDependencies.boundarySemantics: A local subprocess on the same machine, run by the beads adapter alone, told where its state lives through BEADS_DIR: ~/.dotdiw/<key>/.beads under the user's home, keyed to the checkout. It runs in its stealth mode with hooks and agent files declined, so it commits nothing, writes nothing into the repository and configures no remote. The adapter turns its usage metrics off before the first call, rewrites its name in everything it prints, and otherwise changes nothing it does. It has no POA IDL; the commands below are what the adapter calls.
calledOperations: every command dotdiw does not own, forwarded unchanged

externalProductDependencies.reason: git is the registry and the sharing mechanism: a formula the project holds is one git tracks, and it reaches other people as every other file does.
externalProductDependencies.boundarySemantics: The project's own repository, read and never written except two lines inside its .git/config -- the key under which this checkout's tracker lives, and the adapter it was chosen to go through, local to the clone and never in the tree: dotdiw lists tracked and untracked files, reads and unsets one hooks key that an earlier version let the tracker set, and reads status for the declaration files. For a tracker check it makes a scratch repository of its own under a temporary directory and removes it. It never commits, pushes, syncs or changes the index. It has no POA IDL; the commands below are what dotdiw calls.

projections.generator: hand-written: main() in dotdiw parses the affordance, builds the request and calls the operation through the door, invoke, by its id; it installs the presenter that shows each response as its operation returns

poa/finish-idl.py writes the door's table into dotdiw between markers, from operation-idl.json: for every operation, the body's name and the fields of its request and its response, the required ones named. invoke, DoorError and witness_from beside it are hand-written
projections.notes: The one way an operation is invoked, by id and with a request dict. The request is held to its type on the way in and the response to its own on the way out; a key outside either raises DoorError naming the operation and the key. The witness log is appended from the response, and the response is shown by the presenter the interface installs, so every transport runs the same bodies. test_promise.py regenerates the table and fails on any difference.

projections.generator: poa conform grpc-signatures, as a conformance harness only: generated into gitignored gen/ on a machine with Buf; never served

poa/finish-idl.py writes the inner door's table into dotdiw between its own markers, from operation-idl.json: for every operation of the tracker interface, the fields of its request and its response, the required ones named. invoke_tracker, register_tracker and load_tracker beside it are hand-written
projections.notes: The tracker interface as a protocol every adapter implements: a table from operation id to one callable of one request. The registry holds adapters by name; the door resolves the adapter from the request, the workspace's key, or the shipped default, holds both sides to their types, and returns the adapter's records. test_promise.py regenerates the table and fails on any difference.
